$comment: SHARED CROSS-LANGUAGE CONFORMANCE FIXTURE for AUTO-ICONSET-SPEC.md.
Canonical path: TAKPortal/test/fixtures/auto-iconset-golden-vectors.json
This file is the contract for the deterministic iconset identity that ATAK (Java), WinTAK
(C#), CloudTAK (TypeScript) and TAK Portal (JavaScript) must each reproduce BYTE-IDENTICALLY
for the same input. It exists because the audit (C-39) found the TAK Portal implementation
applying the 60-character group cap TWICE, and because no implementation had a single test.
Every value below was produced by the reference implementation
TAKPortal/services/featurelinkArcgisIconset.service.js and is asserted against it by
TAKPortal/test/goldenVectors.test.js. Other work packages: load this file and assert your
port produces the same output. Do NOT regenerate it to make a port pass — a disagreement
means one of the implementations is wrong, and the failure mode in the field is that icons
silently do not resolve on-device.
Reference implementation functions:
canonicalizeUrl(url)      -> spec §2
uidFor(canonicalUrl, fld) -> spec §4
sanitizeGroupBase(name)   -> spec §5.1, the 60-char cap, applied EXACTLY ONCE
groupFor(name)            -> sanitizeGroupBase(name) + ' Icons', max 66 chars
fileNameFor(label)        -> spec §5.2
dedupe(name, seen)        -> spec §5.3

canonicalizeUrl.$comment: §2.1-§2.2. Scheme and host lowercased; path case preserved; query, fragment and trailing slash removed; a service root defaults to layer 0; repeated slashes collapsed. Port is preserved.

cases.name: mixed-case host and a query string
service root with a trailing slash and doubled separators defaults to layer 0
multi-digit layer id, trailing slash removed

mustThrow.name: Web Map item link (§2.3, not resolved here)

uidFor.$comment: §4. Lowercase hex SHA-256 of (canonicalUrl + '/' + fieldName), UTF-8. The LAYER NAME IS NOT AN INPUT — see the c39DoubleTruncation section on what did and did not change.

cases.name: field name case is significant — it is NOT folded

$comment: §5.1. sanitizeGroupBase = replace every character outside [A-Za-z0-9 _-] with '_', collapse
runs of whitespace to one space, trim, then cap at 60. groupFor appends ' Icons', giving a
maximum of 66 characters. THE 60-CHARACTER CAP IS APPLIED EXACTLY ONCE, TO THE BASE, BEFORE
THE SUFFIX. Any implementation that caps the final string at 60 is wrong (that was C-39).
Note 'Damage (2024)' -> 'Damage _2024_ Icons': the spec REPLACES illegal characters with '_'
and does not delete them; the two parentheses become two underscores.

cases.name: latin diacritics are not ASCII and are replaced
CJK is replaced character by character
an emoji is a surrogate PAIR in UTF-16 and becomes TWO underscores
cases.$comment: Java/C#/JS iterate UTF-16 code units here; Python iterates code points and would produce ONE underscore. Every implementation MUST produce two. See crossLanguageNotes.

cases.name: base of exactly 54 -> group of exactly 60, no truncation
THE C-39 CASE: base of 55 -> group of 61. Pre-fix TAK Portal truncated this to 60.
base of exactly 60 -> group of 66, the maximum
base over 60 is cut to 60, then suffixed -> 66
realistic 79-character layer name
cases.in: Damage Assessment Points For Region Seven Central Area Command Post Alpha Bravo
cases.out: Damage Assessment Points For Region Seven Central Area Comma Icons

fileNameFor.$comment: §5.2. Take the last path segment, strip a trailing .png, replace every character outside [A-Za-z0-9._-] with '_', fall back to 'icon' when empty, then append '.png'. There is NO length cap on a filename.

dedupe.$comment: §5.3. Append _2, _3, ... before the .png extension until unique within the set seen so far. Renderer array order is significant, so process entries in the order the renderer lists them.

sequences.name: three identical labels then a distinct one
labels that sanitize to the same filename collide
a slash is a PATH separator in §5.2, not an illegal character — only the last segment survives
sequences.$comment: This is a real cross-implementation trap: 'A/B' does NOT become 'A_B.png'. fileNameFor strips the path prefix first, so it becomes 'B.png' and does not collide with 'A B'.

usericonPath.$comment: §5.4. The on-device reference is exactly '{uid}/{group}/{filename}', joined with '/' and with no escaping or normalisation of any part.

$comment: canonicalizeUrl lowercases the SCHEME and the HOST only; the path keeps its case. Use
toLowerCase(Locale.ROOT) in Java, ToLowerInvariant() in C#, toLowerCase() in JS and lower()
in Python. The vectors below are the JS/Java/Python result.
KNOWN DIVERGENCE, deliberately not papered over: U+0130 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER I WITH DOT
ABOVE lowercases to the TWO code points 'i' + U+0307 in Java (Locale.ROOT), JS and Python,
but .NET's ToLowerInvariant maps it to a single 'i' on some runtimes. This CANNOT affect a
real UID, because the only string canonicalizeUrl case-folds is the host, and DNS/IDNA host
labels are ASCII by the time a URL is parsed. It is recorded so a future port does not
extend case folding to the path or the layer name, where it WOULD diverge.
WHAT CHANGED, precisely — read this before assuming a migration is needed.
The UID DID NOT CHANGE, for any input. uid = SHA-256(canonicalUrl + '/' + field), and the
layer name is not an input to it. Every previously-computed UID is still correct.
What changed is the GROUP — the middle segment of '{uid}/{group}/{filename}'. TAK Portal
capped the group base at 60 in sanitizeGroupBase(), appended ' Icons', and then ran the
result through cleanSetName(), which capped the WHOLE string at 60 again. So for any layer
name whose sanitized base exceeded 54 characters, TAK Portal STORED a 60-character
truncation while ATAK, WinTAK and CloudTAK all produced the full string of up to 66.
Worse, the two halves of TAK Portal disagreed with each other: the truncated value was
returned to the caller as `group`, while the manifest's per-icon groups map was written with
the UNtruncated value — the same request yielded two different group strings.
Threshold: sanitized base length > 54 (i.e. final group length > 60).
Unaffected: base <= 54, which is the overwhelming majority of real layer names.
MIGRATION: no UID migration is required and no config's usericonPath needs rewriting — the
usericonPath already carried the untruncated group. What needs attention is the icon-set
NAME under which affected sets were stored. Regenerating such a layer now registers the set
under the full 66-character name and leaves the old 60-character entry orphaned. Operators
should regenerate affected iconsets and delete the orphaned truncated entries. See
docs/testing/server.md for the detection recipe.
